note: Jared Goff is the QB13 in fantasy points per game. He's having a very strong season, but he'll be tested this week. The Bucs' pass defense has been lights out. Goff could still succeed this week, though. Among 31 qualifying passers, Goff is sixth in yards per attempt, third in passing success rate, 14th in highly accurate throw rate, and third in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, the Bucs have allowed the 11th-lowest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, the third-lowest CPOE, and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Goff has the passing chops, skill players around him, and the excellence against the blitz to still have a strong day in Week 11. Across their last five games, Tampa Bay is second in blitz rate (48.5%) behind only Minnesota. Against the blitz, Goff is fourth in yards per attempt, and he leads all quarterbacks in passing success rate. Goff can still post QB1 numbers this week.

Bo Nix is the QB22 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 19 fantasy points. Outside of his game against Arizona, he hasn't rushed for 15 yards in any other game this season. The reduction in his rushing production has hurt his fantasy floor and ceiling. His passing ability hasn't been able to compensate. Among 31 qualifying passers, Nix is 28th in yards per attempt, 30th in aDOT, 16th in highly accurate throw rate, and 28th in hero throw rate. As bad as Nix is, he might even be able to flirt with QB1 production this week. The Raiders' pass defense has fallen apart. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-most yards per attempt, the second-highest passing touchdown rate, the second-highest passing success rate, and the third-most EPA per dropback.

In a game that could turn into a shootout, Tyler Shough could be a QB1 again this week. Shough is the QB14 in fantasy points per game. Shough has added to his weekly floor and ceiling in the last two games with at least 25 rushing yards in each game. This could coincide with his non-throwing hand healing up. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Shough has been getting it done on the ground and through the air, ranking 15th in passing success rate, 11th in CPOE, and eighth in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, the Bears pass defense has remained a pain point, allowing the sixth-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing touchdown rate, the 13th-highest passing success rate, and the eighth-most fantasy points per dropback.

In his last two starts, Cam Ward has flashed a fantasy pulse as his play has dramatically improved. He has been the QB4 and QB12 in those games in weekly scoring. Let's discuss what has changed for Ward and how he's succeeding. In those games, the Titans have gotten the ball out of his hands quickly while ramping up the RPO rate. Since Week 8, among 28 qualifying quarterbacks, Ward is 17th in passing success rate, 19th in yards per attempt, fifth in highly accurate throw rate, and tenth in catchable target rate. During the same span with the same sample of quarterbacks, Ward also has the lowest aDOT (6.18), the fifth-lowest hero throw rate, the sixth-fastest time to throw, and the highest RPO rate (11.2%; the next closest quarterback is Drew Lock at 7.8%). In those matchups, Ward also wasn't blitzed on 76.4% of his snaps; he saw single high at the eighth-highest rate (59.6%), and he faced the fourth-lowest disguised coverage look. Luckily for Ward, Dallas has the eighth-lowest blitz rate, the seventh-highest single high rate (57.5%), and they are tied for 13th in disguised coverage rate. Ward could flirt with QB1 production again this week against a beatable Dallas pass defense. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 14th-highest passer rating, the 12th-highest CPOE, the ninth-most EPA per dropback, and ranked 15th in passing touchdown rate.

Kirk Cousins is the QB9 in fantasy points per game. In his first start back with the familiar Vikings' purple on his back, he was the QB14 for the week. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Cousins is 12th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 19th in hero throw rate, and 24th in catchable target rate. Cousins is a solid QB2 who could flirt with QB1 production this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the 13th-highest passer rating, the seventh-highest CPOE, and ranked 17th in EPA per dropback.

Overall, Bryce Young is the QB15 in fantasy points per game, but his season has gone off the rails. In his last four games, he has failed to surpass 12 fantasy points in three games, and he is the QB30 in fantasy points per game. During this horrid stretch, among 28 qualifying passers, Young is 24th in yards per attempt, 20th in passing success rate and highly accurate throw rate, 23rd in deep ball rate, and 22nd in hero throw rate. That's a giant grab bag of not good. Young was pushing the ball downfield to begin the season, but that's not happening now, which is also the fallout of his offensive line being terrible during this four-game stretch. In these four games, Young has faced the sixth-highest pressure rate facing defenders in his face on 41.4% of his dropbacks. It's possible that Young bounces back this week, but there's also risk here. On one hand, over their last five games, Baltimore has the second-best pressure rate and the 11th-best quick pressure rate. On the other hand, during that span, Baltimore has also allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the 12th-highest passing touchdown rate, the eighth-highest passing success rate, and the ninth-highest CPOE. Young could play quite well in Week 11, or he could crash and burn if the Ravens' pass rush continually gets home.

Across his last four games, JJ McCarthy has finished as the QB12, QB23, QB26, and QB13 in weekly scoring. The fantasy production hasn't been consistently there because of touchdown output, but McCarthy has played some outstanding football. Among 35 qualifying quarterbacks, McCarthy is third in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, seventh in catchable target rate, first in hero throw rate, and 12th in EPA per dropback. McCarthy will need his A game again this week. The Jags pass defense is no joke. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-fewest yards per attempt, the 14th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the second-lowest passing success rate, and the fourth-lowest EPA per dropback. McCarthy is a QB2 with upside this week if he can overcome the matchup or is tasked with utilizing his legs and rushing upside.

Last week, Justin Herbert had his best game of the season from a fantasy lens. The sad thing is that he only produced 16.3 fantasy points as the QB15 for the week. Most of that fantasy production was tied to his seven rushing attempts, 51 yards on the ground, and a rushing score. That was Herbert's third game with more than 40 rushing yards, but it was his first rushing score. I don't think we can bank on the rushing output weekly from him. Herbert had a middling day as a passer with only 18 passing attempts, 129 passing yards, and zero passing touchdowns. It was nice to see him break the streak of consecutive games with an interception, though. I don't have any faith in Herbert, but I do have plenty of faith that the Jets' pass defense is horrible. If any woeful pass defense can coax a decent QB2 week out of Herbert, it's the Jets. Over their last five games, they have allowed the third-most yards per attempt, the third-highest passing success rate, and the most EPA and fantasy points per dropback.

Aaron Rodgers is the QB20 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying passers, Rodgers is 24th in yards per attempt and passing success rate, 15th in highly accurate throw rate, and 22nd in hero throw rate. Rodgers should deliver decent QB2 production this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the ninth-highest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-most EPA per dropback, and ranked 16th in CPOE.

Last week, in Jacoby Brissett's first start, Baltimore had the sixth-highest pace and led the NFL in passing rate. Ok, that's not what I was expecting at all. Brissett was the QB20 in weekly scoring. He chucked the rock 49 times with 340 passing yards, a 67.3% completion rate, and 6.9 yards per attempt. Baltimore's offensive line allowed him to see pressure on 41.2% of his dropbacks (not good, Bob). Brissett was accurate with the football, with an 83% catchable target rate and 6.1% hero throw rate. Brissett should see more clean pockets this week and walk away with a solid stat line. Over their last five games, Carolina has had the third-lowest pressure rate while allowing the ninth-highest passing success rate, the tenth-highest CPOE, and the 12th-most EPA per dropback. Brissett is a QB2 who could flirt with QB1 production this week.

Geno Smith will be back in the huddle this week. Smith (ankle) got knocked out of last week's game, and his status has been up in the air all week. He had limited practices all week until he upgraded to a full practice on Friday. Smith is QB26 in fantasy points per game with two QB1 games (QB4, QB5) in weekly scoring this season. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Smith is 11th in yards per attempt, 13th in passing success rate, fourth in hero throw rate, and 12th in catchable target rate. Smith is a strong QB2 this week who could be a QB1. The Bolts' pass defense has been lacking all season. Over their last five games, the Chargers have allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the tenth-highest passing success rate, and the 14th-highest EPA and fantasy points per dropback.

In his only start this season, Joe Milton finished as the QB18 for the week with nine rushing attempts and 64 yards on the ground, fueling his fantasy output. Milton remains a work in progress as a passer. He completed 52.9% of his passes with 169 yards through the air (5.0 yards per attempt). 32.4% of his passes were off-target, and he had only a 55.9% highly accurate throw rate. Milton remains a low-end QB2 this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the sixth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the tenth-lowest CPOE.

In his first NFL start, Fernando Mendoza was the QB18 in weekly scoring. Much of his fantasy scoring was related to his 22 rushing yards and rushing score. He finished with only 29 passing attempts, 143 passing yards (zero passing touchdowns), and 4.9 yards per attempt. Mendoza had a 55.2% highly accurate throw rate, a 77.8% catchable target rate, and he threw to his first read on only 34.5% of his plays. Overall, nothing amazing but also nothing horrible there considering it was his first start and against Seattle. Mendoza has another rough matchup this week. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the eighth-fewest yards per attempt, the 12th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the tenth-lowest EPA per dropback, and the 11th-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Last week, Kyle McCord finished as the QB20 in weekly scoring. He completed 53.1% of his passes with 209 passing yards, only a 34.4% successful play rate, a 46.9% highly accurate throw rate, and a horrible 21.9% off-target rate. McCord was aggressive, though, with a 21.9% deep ball rate, a 10.4 aDOT, anda 6.3% hero throw rate. His rushing touchdown (only two rushing attempts and four rushing yards) carried his fantasy day, but I wouldn't depend on that going forward. McCord is headed toward a long day in Week 11 against an improved Buffalo pass defense. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 11th-lowest passing success rate, the lowest CPOE, and the sixth-lowest EPA per dropback.

Daniel Jones is the QB31 in fantasy points per game. He hasn't posted more than 12.5 fantasy points in a game since Week 6, which was the only time that has happened all season. Last week, in a wonderful matchup against the Dolphins, Jones struggled with a 50% completion rate, 108 passing yards, 4.9 yards per attempt, and two picks (two passing touchdowns as well). I have zero faith in Jones at this point to produce, even when the matchup is in his favor. Sit him.

Baker Mayfield (foot/right thumb) managed limited practices on Thursday and Friday and has been listed as questionable. I still lean toward Jalon Daniels starting this week, but I want to make sure fantasy managers are equipped with Mayfield info if I'm wrong and he does start this week. Mayfield has been a disaster as a passer since returning from the thumb injury. Against Carolina, he had only 11 passing attempts with 64 passing yards (5.8 yards per attempt). In Week 8, he famously had three passing attempts and zero passing yards. Against the Bears in Week 9, Mayfield had his "strongest" passing day, completing 56.3% of his passes with 243 passing yards (7.6 yards per attempt) and zero passing touchdowns (two interceptions). Overall, since his return, he has only 6.6 yards per attempt, a 39.1% passing success rate, a 43.5% highly accurate throw rate, and a 21.7% off-target rate. All of those numbers are dumpster-fire-level passing accuracy. Mayfield will be headed for another long day if he starts in Week 11. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest CPOE, the 13th-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback.

Last week, Carson Beck (in his first NFL start) finished as the QB30 in weekly scoring with only 2.4 fantasy points. Beck passed for only 108 yards with 6.0 yards per attempt, zero passing touchdowns, and two picks. I have zero interest in playing Beck this week in any format. The Chiefs have been a nightmare matchup for quarterbacks. In their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing touchdown rate, the lowest passing success rate, and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

With Baker Mayfield dealing with a foot sprain, I'm expecting Jalon Daniels to start for Tampa Bay this week. I'll update the entire Bucs offensive outlook on Friday if I'm wrong about this. Daniels has been a solid QB2 in his three starts this season as the QB21, QB19, and QB22 in weekly scoring. The Bucs tried to limit his passing volume in those three starts, as he never exceeded 200 passing yards in any start and only once did he exceed 27 passing attempts. He did contribute on the ground, averaging 6.3 rushing attempts and 39 rushing yards (zero rushing scores). This season, among 37 qualifying passers, Daniels is 37th in yards per attempt, 35th in passing success rate, 37th in CPOE, and 32nd in catchable target rate. Yes, the Lions lost Aidan Hutchinson last week, which will impact their pass rush, but their pass defense has been stout recently. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest CPOE, the 13th-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback. Daniels is a low-end QB2 this week.

In his last two games, Cam Skattebo has been the RB6 and RB10 in weekly scoring while averaging 19.5 touches and 121.5 total yards. In those games, he has had a 72.1% snap rate, 57.4% of the rushing work, and a 46.5% route share (7.8% target share). I expect him to have a similar workload this week. Among 51 qualifying rushers, Skattebo is 18th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Against an elite run defense this week that will unveil Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, Skattebo is a volume-based RB2. Across their last five games, the Jags have allowed the seventh-lowest rushing success rate while logging the fourth-highest hit rate at or behind the line of scrimmage and ranking 16th in yards after contact per attempt.

Jonathan Taylor is the RB11 in fantasy points per game, despite the Colts' broken team and offense. Last week, he played 66.7% of the snaps with 47.1% of the rushing work and a 76% route share (18.2% target share). Taylor is still splitting early down work with Seth McGowan despite the Colts refusing to trade him. He has a strong 13.9% explosive run rate and 18% missed tackle rate. Despite Daniel Jones, Taylor should still produce RB1/2 numbers this week. Houston's run defense has been more pliable recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the 12th-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, the Jets' backfield tilted back further in favor of Breece Hall. Hall finished with a 58.8% snap rate, 47.8% of the rushing work, and a 43.8% route share. Those numbers all eclipsed Braelon Allen's usage. Hall finished with 15 touches and 108 total yards. Hall has only managed a woeful 1.66 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate this season. He's a volume play at running back again this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have fielded a middle-of-the-road run defense, allowing the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt while ranking 16th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt, 15th in rushing success rate, and 18th in missed tackle rate.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.1 touches and 89.8 total yards. Last week, with Kyle McCord under center, Gordon saw a nice bump in his passing game usage with a 12.1% target share, a 21% TPRR, and 39 receiving yards. It was his highest receiving yardage output of the season and his second-highest target share and TPRR of the season. If Gordon is going to see some checkdowns weekly, it'll be a huge add to his weekly floor and ceiling. Prior to last week's game, he hadn't had more than 14 receiving yards in any game this season. Among 51 qualifying backs, Gordon is 12th in explosive run rate and 30th in missed tackle rate. Gordon should have another solid week. Over their last five games, Buffalo has ranked 18th in yards after contact per attempt while allowing the sixth-highest rushing success rate and missed tackle rate.

David Montgomery will be back this week. With Woody Marks out, I expect Montgomery to lead the backfield in touches this week, but we'll likely see Emari Demercado mixed in. Montgomery hasn't been effective when on the field this season. He has only a 2.1% explosive run rate, 1.65 yards after contact per attempt, and a 13% missed tackle rate. The context that needs to be applied here, though, is that the offensive line has given him zero room to operate with only 1.00 yards before contact per attempt on his carries, and he has been hit at the line or behind it with 53.8% of his carries. Montgomery should have some room to get loose this week, though. The Colts' run defense has fallen apart. Over their last two games, they have allowed the ninth-most rushing yards, the ninth-highest explosive run rate, and the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt. Montgomery should see 12-15 touches in this game and return decent RB2 production.

I expect Saquon Barkley to be back to his workhorse status this week. He opened this week with a full practice. In his last game played, he had a 57.6% snap rate, 52% of the rushing work, and a 31.3% route share (2.9% target share). Barkley finished with a disappointing 13 touches and 22 total yards. This season, he has logged a disappointing 2.04 yards after contact per attempt with a respectable 17% missed tackle rate. Barkley is a volume-driven RB2 option this week with a tough matchup. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, and the 11th-fewest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate.

Last week, Omarion Hampton had EASILY his best game of the 2026 season as the RB13 for the week. Hampton had 23 touches (22 carries), 105 total yards, and a score. That's the positive news. Ok, now it's time for the bad. Hampton played 63% of the snaps in a game that they played with a lead in. He had 64.7% of the rushing work, BUT he had only a 33% route share, which equaled the route share for Keaton Mitchell and was behind Kimani Vidal (40.7%). This all quietly says that Hampton is game script sensitive and could still be crushed in any game moving forward in which the Bolts are trailing. It's sad, but true. The good thing for Hampton is hopefully the Bolts are playing with a lead this week, and it's a nice matchup for him on the ground. Hampton has 2.22 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate this season (OOF!). The Jets still have a woeful run defense, so hopefully Hampton can take advantage. Over their last five games, the Jets have allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Since his soft benching in Week 8, Ashton Jeanty has reclaimed his lead back role for the Raiders. Their horrible offensive line hasn't allowed for any more running room or production, though. In his last two games, Jeanty has played 68.9% of the snaps with a 60.6% route share (18% target share). He has averaged 12 touches and 42 total yards (zero touchdowns). Jeanty has only a 4.5% explosive run rate, 2.11 yards after contact per attempt, and an 11% missed tackle rate. Jeanty is just a volume-driven flex with a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the tenth-lowest rushing success rate, the 14th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Since Week 7, Aaron Jones has averaged 8.6 touches and 35.6 total yards while seeing five of the backfield's eight red zone rushing attempts. During this stretch of games, Jones has had a 36.9% snap rate, 32.2% of the rushing work, and a 25% route share (4.3% target share). He has taken a back seat in each of those categories to Jordan Mason. Jones hasn't been much more efficient than Mason, with only 2.04 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Jones is a desperation touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have held backs to the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Kyle Monangai opened this week with a full practice (toe). I'm expecting him to be back this week. Monangai is the RB17 in fantasy points per game, averaging 16.3 touches and 90.8 total yards. Among 51 qualifying backs, Monangai is eighth in explosive run rate, first in yards after contact per attempt, and 12th in missed tackle rate. Monangai should have another nice outing this week. Over their last five games, the Saints have ranked 17th in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate and zone rushing success rate (Monangai: 70% zone).

Since Week 6, Rachaad White has been the RB34 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11.3 touches and 59.6 total yards. Overall this season, among 51 qualifying backs, White is 35th in yards after contact per attempt and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Since Week 6, he has had a 56.4% snap rate, 37.9% of the rushing work (losing carries to Austin Ekeler), and a 39.1% route share (9.5% target share). I know Cincy looked like an imposing run defense last week, but I need to see it again before I'm willing to fade a running back facing them. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the second-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-highest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt. UPDATE: Bill might be back this week. I'll update the status of this backfield on Saturday. Also, White had a limited practice (heel) on Friday.

Since Week 7, Rico Dowdle has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 12.4 touches and 58.7 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 46.7% snap rate, 33.7% of the rushing work, and a 47.9% route share (9.2% target share). Dowdle has been impressive on a per-touch basis this season with 2.69 yards after contact per attempt and a 22% missed tackle rate. Dowdle is a strong flex option again this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Travis Etienne still operated in a three-way committee in his first game back. Etienne played only 34.4% of the snaps with a 34.8% rushing share (led the team) and a 27.9% route share (8.6% target share. Audric Estime, Alvin Kamara, and Etienne split the red zone work with each back seeing a red zone rushing attempt and a 33.3% snap rate. Etienne finished with 11 touches and 34 total yards. With only 1.79 yards after contact per attempt, a 16% missed tackle rate, and confusing usage, Etienne is only a middling flex. Even with Jeffrey Simmons, the Bears' run defense has remained bad allowing the 12th-highest explosive run rate, the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Jordan Mason has averaged 13.1 touches and 47.3 total yards while seeing three of the backfield's eight red zone rushing attempts. During this span of four games, Mason has had a 48.4% snap rate, a 50% rushing share, and a 27.3% route share (5.2% target share). Mason has been dreadfully inefficient this season with only 2.00 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate. Mason is a desperation touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have held backs to the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week, with Bam Knight back, Tyler Allgeier took a backseat with a 44.1% snap rate, 45.5% of the rushing work, and only a 16.7% route share (5.6% target share). Allgeier had only five touches and 14 total yards. Allgeier has been woefully inefficient this season with only a 6.9% explosive run rate and 10% missed tackle rate. Allgeier is a sit this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 12th-lowest explosive run rate, the ninth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Braelon Allen saw his workload cut further as Breece Hall resumed his lead back duties for New York. Allen played 47.1% of the snaps with 34.8% of the rushing work and a 37.5% route share (2.4% target share). Allen finished with nine touches and 46 total yards. The reduction in work has put him back in the touchdown-dependent flex area code again. Allen has still been amazing on a per-touch basis with 2.70 yards after contact per attempt and a 20% missed tackle rate, but with his volume being limited, it's tough to expect more than flex production out of him. Over their last five games, the Bolts have fielded a middle-of-the-road run defense, allowing the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt while ranking 16th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt, 15th in rushing success rate, and 18th in missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Kenneth Gainwell has been the RB28 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.7 touches and 101.3 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 39.7% snap rate, 33.1% of the rushing work, and a 30.8% route share (8.7% target share). Gainwell has been amazing on a per-touch basis with a 14.5% explosive run rate, 2.94 yards after contact per attempt, and a 27% missed tackle rate. The Detroit run defense will suffer without Aidan Hutchinson, but I expect them to remain strong against the run. This means Gainwell is only a middling flex option this week. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the second-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the fifth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week, Alvin Kamara played only 16 snaps (25.4% snap rate) with five touches and 14 total yards. Yes, he scored two touchdowns, but I can't depend on that weekly. Across his previous four games, Kamara scored only once. With his snap rate declining with Travis Etienne back and Audric Estime in the mix, I can't trust Kamara even as a flex option this week.

Bam Knight returned to the lineup last week. While he finished with only five touches and 19 total yards, he was the backfield leader. Knight led the backfield with a 55.9% snap rate and 50% route share (5.6% target share). He split the early down work evenly with Tyler Allgeier, with each back seeing five carries (45.5% of the rushing work). Knight has been strong with his 33 carries this season with a 17.2% explosive run rate, 2.88 yards after contact per attempt, and a 24% missed tackle rate. Knight is a low-end flex this week, only reserved for desperation or deeper leagues. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 12th-lowest explosive run rate, the ninth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Over the last three games, Kaelon Black has seen a bump in his role, averaging 12.3 touches and 65 total yards. He has scored touchdowns in two of those three games. The talented rookie runs like an overly caffeinated hedgehog. If you want a perfect example of his max effort running style, just search his name and Dallas Cowboys. His per-touch metrics have improved as we have moved through the season, with 2.51 yards after contact per attempt and a 16% missed tackle rate. He could easily see 10-12 touches and get in the endzone again this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has ranked 16th in explosive run rate while allowing the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Seth McGowan is a flex option this week. Over the last two games, he has averaged 9.5 touches and 59.5 total yards with a score in each game. McGowan has been amazing on a per-touch basis this season. He has 3.22 yards after contact per attempt and an insane 27% missed tackle rate. He could get into the endzone this week and pay off for fantasy again. Houston's run defense has been more pliable recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the 12th-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Garrett Wilson is the WR20 in fantasy points per game, sporting a 27.5% target share with 2.18 YPRR, eight red zone targets, 13 deep targets, and a 34.7% first-read share. There was some debate in the middle of the season, but Wilson is their undisputed WR1. The on-paper matchup is glorious. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. With Geno Smith back, Wilson is a top-15 wide receiver this week with WR1 upside.

Tetairoa McMillan's production has been crushed, with Bryce Young struggling behind a woeful offensive line. Since Week 7, McMillan has been the WR39 in fantasy points per game. In these four games, he has had a 20.6% target share with 1.40 YPRR, two red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 28% first-read share. This could be a bounce-back game for Young, which should fuel McMillan's stat line. Across their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since his Week 8 return, DJ Moore has been the WR19 in fantasy points per game with a 20.9% target share, 2.74 YPRR, three red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. He has surpassed 80 receiving yards and scored a touchdown in two of those three games. Moore should crush again this week. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, with Josh Downs playing, Rashee Rice had a 17.1% target share, 82 receiving yards (3.57 YPRR), a 19% first-read share, and he ran 69.6% of his routes from the perimeter. I expect his usage as an outside receiver to continue as Downs takes the slot role. Rice still had a 33.3% designed target rate, but he also had a 9.17 aDOT, so it wasn't just low aDOT gadget stuff. Rice was the WR23 in weekly scoring. Rice could easily be a WR2 again this week.
